subject: Biology
title: Egg and Sperm: Cells of Creation
description: One-minute skill: Egg and Sperm: Cells of Creation.

hook.text: The human egg cell is the body's largest—visible to the naked eye at 0.1 millimeters.

buildup.text: Sperm cells are tiny, stripped to just DNA, a tail, and mitochondria for fuel.

discovery.text: When sperm meets egg, two half-sets of chromosomes unite into a full set of 46.

twist.text: Of roughly 250 million sperm released, typically only one fertilizes the egg.

climax.text: That single fertilized cell divides into every cell type in a human body.

punchline.text: Two half-cells make a whole new person.

quiz.question: What is the largest cell in the human body?

details.summary: Egg and sperm are highly specialized reproductive cells produced by meiosis. The egg is the largest human cell, packed with nutrients and organelles, while sperm is one of the smallest, streamlined for delivering DNA. Their fusion at fertilization creates a new organism.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding gamete biology is essential for reproductive medicine, fertility treatments, and contraception. The mechanisms of egg-sperm recognition and fusion also illuminate fundamental questions about how organisms develop.
takeaways: The egg is the largest human cell; sperm is among the smallest
Both carry half the chromosomes needed for a complete organism
Fertilization restores the full chromosome number and triggers development

faq.question: Why is the egg so much larger than the sperm?
faq.answer: The egg provides all the cytoplasm, organelles, nutrients, and molecular machinery needed for early embryonic development. Sperm contributes essentially only DNA. This asymmetry reflects their different roles: the egg nourishes while the sperm delivers genetic material.

faq.question: How does the egg prevent multiple sperm from fertilizing it?
faq.answer: When one sperm fuses with the egg, immediate chemical changes called the cortical reaction modify the egg's outer layer, creating a barrier that blocks additional sperm. Polyspermy would introduce too many chromosomes and is lethal to the embryo.
